# The completion gate cannot verify a large epic: step budget exhausts at 480 AND at 1600

## The failure

Closing epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb] (59 descendants, all closed and certified) fails:

    Error: cannot close e369-a449-4773-48fb: completion verification could not run
    (completion verification workflow did not produce a verdict: step 'decide@then/verify' failed:
     agent exceeded its step budget (max_iterations=480; ~1 model request per tool call).
     Raise REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS or narrow the task.)

Retried with `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=1600` (3.3x the default). **Exhausted again**, after ~50 minutes,
identical message, `max_iterations=1600`.

## MEASURED root cause (rebar-debug Phase 1 — see the RCA comment)

An instrumented reproduction (every agent tool call logged; 264 calls, 1074s, `max_iterations=480`)
settled the question by measurement: **the verifier LOOPS; it does not converge at any budget.**
Novelty by quartile: calls 1-132 are 94-98% novel, calls 199-264 are **0% novel**. From call #121
(t=537s) the agent is in a closed 4-call cycle repeated 31-37x against a single file.

The loop's engine is a tool defect: **`search_files` silently returns `"(no matches)"` when its
`path` argument names a FILE rather than a directory** (and likewise for a path that does not
exist). `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py:107` walks `os.walk(base)`; `os.walk` on a file yields nothing,
so control falls through to `return "\n".join(hits) or "(no matches)"` at `pai_tools.py:140`. There
is no file/directory discrimination and no existence check.

Ground-truthed live in-run false negatives: `search_files("J1", ".../test_backend_characterization.py")`
-> `(no matches)` while `J1` is on line 116 of that file (this is the loop); `allow_insecure` in
`src/rebar/_config_schema.py` -> `(no matches)` with **21 real hits**; `resolved_statuses` in the same
file -> `(no matches)` with 5 real hits. Aggregate: **48% of `search_files` calls passed a file path,
100% of those returned `(no matches)`, and 26 of 29 had the literal genuinely present** — 29% of every
tool call in the run was a guaranteed-false negative.

Beyond the wasted budget this is a **false-FAIL vector on a signed gate**: the packaged
`completion-verifier` prompt tells the agent that `(no matches)` means "only that *that literal
string* is absent", and encourages narrowing the search path — the exact move that returns a lie.

## Scope of THIS ticket

This ticket fixes **only** the `search_files` path-handling defect. It is the smallest change that
removes the loop's fuel and closes the signed-gate false-FAIL vector. Four further defects were
proven in the same investigation and are filed separately (linked `discovered_from` this ticket)
because each changes gate control flow or operator messaging and deserves its own review:

* no loop breaker — `RunRequest.tool_step_limit` is never set for the primary verify step;
* the bounded completion recovery is unreachable for a step-budget `LLMRunnerError`;
* the repetition diagnostic is computed and then dropped (no `gate_error_v1` sidecar);
* the close gate offers `--force-close` as the remedy for a RESOURCE exhaustion.

`read_file`'s inverted-range fallback (`pai_tools.py:63`) is also deliberately **out of scope**: it
was not part of the proven mechanism (the inverted read actually returned text containing the sought
literal), and changing a second function's contract in this repo-wide shared module would materially
widen the review surface. Filed separately.

## The fix

In `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py`, `search_files` must resolve its `path` argument before walking:

* `path` names an existing **file** -> scan that single file and return its `file:line: text` hits,
  applying the same discovery filter and `_SEARCH_MAX_HITS` cap as the directory walk;
* `path` names an existing **directory** -> **unchanged** `os.walk` behaviour (every existing caller
  depends on this; the contract must not move);
* `path` does not exist -> return an explicit `Error: ...` string, never `"(no matches)"`, so an
  agent can tell "I mistyped the path" from "the literal is absent".

`"(no matches)"` must from now on mean exactly one thing: the literal was searched for and is absent.

## Blast radius

`pai_tools.py` supplies the read-only tools to **every** LLM gate (plan-review, code-review,
completion), so the change is repo-wide in effect even though the diff is one function. The
directory-path branch is therefore held byte-identical in behaviour and is pinned by a regression
test, and the change is additive: it converts two cases that currently return a false
`"(no matches)"` into a true hit list and an explicit error respectively. No caller passes a file
path today expecting `"(no matches)"` — that value is indistinguishable from the honest-absence
answer, so nothing can be relying on it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `search_files(query, path)` where `path` names an existing FILE that contains `query` returns
      the `file:line: text` hit(s), not `"(no matches)"`
- [ ] `search_files(query, path)` where `path` names an existing FILE that does NOT contain `query`
      still returns `"(no matches)"` (honest absence is preserved)
- [ ] `search_files(query, path)` where `path` names a DIRECTORY is unchanged — same hits, same
      ordering, same caps (regression pin; every existing gate depends on it)
- [ ] `search_files(query, path)` where `path` does not exist returns an explicit `Error: ...`,
      never `"(no matches)"`
- [ ] the repo-root confinement and deny-list of `_safe_path` still apply to a file path — a file
      outside the root or on the deny-list is refused exactly as a directory is
- [ ] the RED test is shown failing for the right reason before the fix and passing after, and the
      full CI selection (`pytest -m "not integration and not external"`) stays green

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/test_pai_tools_search_files_bf31.py -q
    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q
